The decks and aisles are configured to define a rolling surface for an autonomous transport vehicle at each deck level. Racks along at least one aisle at each level include multiple rack levels accessed from a respective rolling surface common to the multiple rack levels. A vertical pitch between rack levels varies along a portion of a respective aisle, and the vertical pitch between at least two rack levels of that portion of the respective aisle is related to another vertical pitch between at least two other rack levels of another aisle portion of the respective aisle, such that the vehicle effects multiple picks in an ordered sequence during a common aisle pass.
outputs.L2: An automated storage and retrieval system has a storage array made up of rack-mounted storage locations arranged beside picking aisles and across multiple deck levels. At least one deck is connected to each aisle, and the decks together with the aisles form travel surfaces for an autonomous transport vehicle at the respective deck levels. Along at least one aisle on each level, the racks include several rack tiers that can be reached from the same corresponding travel surface. For part of a given aisle, the vertical spacing between rack tiers is not uniform. The spacing between at least two rack tiers in that aisle portion is coordinated with the spacing between at least two different rack tiers in another portion of the same aisle, allowing the vehicle to perform multiple picks in a prescribed order during a single pass through the aisle.
outputs.L3:
The storage array forms part of an automated storage and retrieval system in which storage spaces are arranged on racks positioned along one or more picking aisles. These aisles define travel paths through the system and allow items stored in the racks to be accessed and retrieved in an organized manner.

The system includes multiple level decks that communicate with the picking aisles. Each level deck provides a rolling surface on which autonomous transport vehicles can travel. These vehicles are configured to move along the aisles, access the storage racks, and perform picking operations without requiring manual intervention.

Along at least one of the picking aisles, the racks include multiple rack levels that are accessible from a common rolling surface. In other words, an autonomous transport vehicle traveling on the same deck or travel surface can reach storage locations positioned at different vertical levels within the rack structure.

The vertical spacing between the rack levels is not necessarily uniform along the entire aisle. Instead, the spacing may vary along different portions of the aisle to accommodate different item sizes, storage requirements, or picking patterns. Some portions of the aisle may have closely spaced rack levels for smaller items, while other portions may provide greater vertical spacing for larger items or containers.

This variable rack-level spacing is configured to support efficient picking by the autonomous transport vehicle. In particular, the spacing and arrangement of the rack levels allow the vehicle to perform multiple picks in a predetermined or ordered sequence during a single pass along the aisle. As a result, the vehicle can retrieve multiple items without repeatedly entering and exiting the same aisle, improving throughput, reducing travel time, and increasing the overall efficiency of the automated storage and retrieval system.
outputs.L4:
An automated storage and retrieval system is provided for storing and retrieving goods, containers, totes, trays, or other load carriers in a highly efficient manner. The system includes a storage structure having a plurality of vertically spaced decks, a plurality of aisles extending through the storage structure, and a plurality of rack levels arranged along the aisles. Autonomous transport vehicles travel within the storage structure to access storage locations and to perform picking, placing, replenishment, or retrieval operations.

Each aisle may include one or more rolling surfaces that support and guide the autonomous transport vehicles. In certain portions of the storage structure, the rolling surfaces are shared by multiple rack levels or are positioned so that a vehicle traveling along a common aisle path can access storage locations at more than one vertical level. The rack levels are not necessarily spaced at a uniform vertical pitch throughout the entire aisle. Instead, the vertical distance, or pitch, between adjacent rack levels may vary along different portions of an aisle. For example, a first aisle portion may have rack levels separated by a first vertical pitch, while a second aisle portion may have rack levels separated by a different vertical pitch. These pitch variations may be selected based on the dimensions of the stored items, the configuration of the vehicles, the required access positions, or the desired picking sequence.

The rack level pitch relationships are arranged to coordinate with the movement and picking capability of the autonomous transport vehicles. In particular, the vertical spacing between rack levels may be selected so that a vehicle traveling along a single aisle pass can access multiple rack levels in a predetermined order. This allows the vehicle to perform two or more ordered picks without needing to leave the aisle, change decks, reverse direction, or make separate passes for each item. The vehicle may therefore collect several items from different rack levels or storage positions during one continuous or substantially continuous movement through the aisle.

In one example, an autonomous transport vehicle enters an aisle and travels along a rolling surface shared by adjacent storage levels. As it progresses through the aisle, it encounters storage locations arranged at different vertical positions. Because the pitch between these rack levels has been coordinated with the vehicle’s access mechanism, the vehicle can retrieve a first item from a first rack level, continue along the same aisle, retrieve a second item from a second rack level, and optionally retrieve additional items from further rack levels. The sequence of picks may correspond to an order profile, a batch picking operation, a replenishment task, or another warehouse control instruction.

By enabling multiple ordered picks during a single common aisle pass, the system reduces unnecessary travel, improves vehicle utilization, and increases overall throughput. The arrangement may also reduce congestion within the storage structure because fewer vehicle movements are required to complete the same number of picking tasks. In addition, the ability to vary rack level pitch along aisle portions permits the storage structure to accommodate different product sizes and storage densities while maintaining efficient access by the autonomous vehicles.

The system may be controlled by a warehouse management system, warehouse control system, or other automated controller that assigns tasks to the autonomous transport vehicles. The controller may determine an optimized travel path and pick sequence based on item location, vehicle availability, order priority, rack level pitch, aisle configuration, and deck accessibility. The controller may then direct a vehicle to perform a common aisle pass in which multiple required items are picked in an ordered sequence. The vehicle may include sensors, navigation equipment, lifting or transfer mechanisms, and onboard control systems that allow it to position itself accurately relative to the selected storage locations.

Overall, the automated storage and retrieval system combines multi-level storage decks, aisle-based travel paths, shared rolling surfaces, and deliberately arranged vertical pitch relationships between rack levels. This configuration enables autonomous transport vehicles to perform multiple coordinated picking operations during a single aisle traversal. As a result, the system can provide improved picking efficiency, higher storage density, reduced travel time, and increased productivity in automated warehouse and fulfillment environments.
outputs.L5:
A storage array is a centralized system designed to store, manage, and protect large amounts of digital data. It is commonly used by businesses, data centers, and organizations that need reliable access to files, applications, databases, and backup information. Unlike a single hard drive or server, a storage array contains multiple storage devices that work together to provide higher capacity, better performance, and improved data protection.

A storage array may use hard disk drives, solid-state drives, or a combination of both. Many modern storage arrays include advanced features such as data replication, snapshots, encryption, compression, and automatic failover. These tools help ensure that information remains available even if a drive or component fails.

There are different types of storage arrays, including all-flash arrays, hybrid arrays, and traditional disk-based arrays. All-flash storage arrays are known for high speed and low latency, making them ideal for demanding applications and virtual environments. Hybrid arrays combine flash and disk storage to balance performance and cost.

Businesses use a storage array to support critical workloads, improve data access, and simplify storage management. By consolidating data into a single, scalable platform, organizations can reduce complexity and prepare for future growth. A well-designed storage array is an important part of a modern IT infrastructure, helping companies keep their data secure, organized, and available when needed.

counterfactuals.prompt: Write a legalistic patent-style description of an AS/RS storage array where autonomous transport vehicles travel on deck rolling surfaces and access multiple rack levels with variable vertical pitch to enable ordered multiple picks.
counterfactuals.output:
An automated storage and retrieval system (AS/RS) is provided comprising a storage array having a plurality of storage racks arranged in rows defining aisles therebetween, a plurality of deck structures defining vehicle-travel surfaces at one or more elevations, and a fleet of autonomous transport vehicles configured to travel along the deck structures and access storage locations disposed at a plurality of rack levels. The storage racks include vertically spaced load-support locations configured to receive totes, trays, cartons, pallets, bins, containers, or other storage units. The vertical spacing, or pitch, between adjacent rack levels is selectively variable within the storage array, such that different zones, rack bays, rack columns, or storage levels may have different vertical pitches corresponding to different article heights, storage-unit dimensions, order profiles, or picking sequences.

In one embodiment, the AS/RS comprises a framework including upright members, horizontal beams, and deck panels or rails forming substantially planar rolling surfaces upon which the autonomous transport vehicles are supported. The deck rolling surfaces may extend along aisles, cross-aisles, transfer regions, staging regions, or pick faces. Each autonomous transport vehicle includes a drive system, a navigation system, an onboard controller, and a load-handling mechanism configured to transfer a storage unit between the vehicle and a selected storage location. The vehicle may include wheels, rollers, casters, or track-engaging elements adapted to move over the deck rolling surface without requiring a suspended carriage, fixed crane mast, or continuous rail-mounted shuttle at each rack level.

The storage array is configured such that a transport vehicle travelling on a given deck rolling surface may access more than one vertical rack level. In certain embodiments, the vehicle includes a vertically displaceable load handler, lift table, telescoping extractor, articulated transfer mechanism, shuttle arm, fork assembly, or gripper assembly having a vertical working range sufficient to reach a plurality of rack levels positioned above and/or below the deck rolling surface. Accordingly, a single travel deck may service multiple rack levels, thereby reducing the number of decks, rails, or vehicle lanes required for a given storage height.

The vertical pitch between rack levels may be non-uniform. For example, a first region of the storage array may include closely spaced rack levels configured for low-height containers, while a second region may include larger pitch spacing configured for taller containers or mixed-height inventory. In further embodiments, the pitch may vary along a vertical column, along a rack row, between adjacent bays, or between different storage zones. The system controller may maintain a map of rack-level elevations and pitch values, and may assign storage and retrieval tasks based at least in part on the vertical reach capability of available vehicles, the location of the deck rolling surface, the height of a storage unit, and a desired order sequence.

The autonomous transport vehicles may be operated to perform ordered multiple picks. In such operation, a vehicle receives a task list including a plurality of storage locations corresponding to items or storage units required for one or more customer orders, production batches, replenishment tasks, or outbound sequences. The vehicle travels on the deck rolling surface through the storage array and accesses selected storage locations at different rack levels without returning to a central lift, workstation, or discharge point between each pick. The vehicle may retrieve multiple storage units in a predetermined order, or may retrieve individual items from multiple presented storage units according to a pick sequence generated by a warehouse control system.

In one embodiment, the vehicle includes a load-carrying platform having capacity for a plurality of storage units. The controller directs the vehicle to a first rack location at a first rack level, actuates the load-handling mechanism to retrieve a first storage unit, then directs the vehicle to a second rack location at a second rack level having a different elevation. The second rack level may be separated from the first rack level by a pitch that differs from the pitch between other adjacent rack levels in the array. The vehicle may thereafter retrieve additional storage units from additional rack levels or bays, thereby forming an ordered group of picks on the vehicle. The ordered group may correspond to a delivery sequence required at a downstream workstation, packing station, sorter, robotic picking cell, manual pick station, kitting area, or outbound conveyor.

The deck rolling surfaces may be disposed at intermediate elevations relative to the rack levels. For example, a deck rolling surface may be positioned between an upper rack level and a lower rack level, enabling the same vehicle to access storage locations both above and below the deck. In another embodiment, the deck rolling surface is positioned adjacent a plurality of rack levels on one or both sides of an aisle, and the vehicle load handler moves vertically relative to the vehicle chassis to align with the selected level. The deck may comprise continuous flooring, discrete running strips, rails, gratings, composite panels, metal plates, or modular deck segments supported by the rack framework or by an independent support structure.

The AS/RS may further include vertical transfer devices, ramps, elevators, lifts, hoists, spiral conveyors, or inclined travel paths configured to move vehicles or storage units between deck elevations. In some embodiments, however, multiple rack levels are serviced from a single deck elevation, thereby reducing reliance on vertical transfer devices and improving throughput for multi-line orders. A vehicle may be assigned to a zone of the array based on its vertical access envelope, current load status, energy level, proximity to required picks, and the ordered sequence in which the picks are to be delivered.

A control system is operatively coupled to the autonomous transport vehicles and maintains data representative of: storage-unit identity, storage-unit height, rack-location coordinates, rack-level elevation, rack-level pitch, deck elevation, vehicle position, vehicle load state, and order priority. The control system may generate a route and pick sequence that causes a vehicle to collect storage units from levels having variable pitch while preserving an ordered arrangement of the collected units. In certain embodiments, the vehicle includes multiple load positions, and the controller selects which load position receives each retrieved storage unit so that the storage units are later discharged in a predetermined sequence. Alternatively, the vehicle may retrieve and discharge storage units one at a time while following an ordered route among multiple rack levels.

The variable vertical pitch may be dynamically configurable or structurally adjustable. Rack beams may be mountable at selected elevations along uprights having hole patterns, slots, brackets, or modular attachment points. During installation or reconfiguration, rack levels may be repositioned to accommodate changes in inventory profile. The system controller may be updated to reflect modified elevations, thereby allowing the autonomous vehicles to continue accessing multiple rack levels from the deck rolling surfaces without requiring uniform rack spacing throughout the facility.

In another embodiment, the deck rolling surface includes localization features, fiducial markers, magnetic elements, optical codes, RFID tags, embedded conductors, guide rails, or machine-readable references enabling the autonomous transport vehicle to determine its position relative to rack bays and rack levels. The vehicle may use such position information, together with stored pitch data, to align the load-handling mechanism with a target rack location. Sensors on the vehicle may verify the presence, absence, size, or alignment of a storage unit before transfer.

The system thereby provides a storage array in which autonomous transport vehicles travel on deck rolling surfaces and access multiple vertically spaced rack levels having non-uniform pitch. By enabling a vehicle to retrieve multiple storage units or items from different levels in an ordered sequence, the system improves storage density, reduces travel and transfer time, supports mixed-height inventory, and increases order-fulfillment throughput relative to systems requiring a dedicated vehicle path at each rack level or uniform vertical rack spacing throughout the array.

counterfactuals.prompt: Create dense patent claim language for a storage rack array with multiple deck levels, autonomous transport vehicle rolling surfaces, racks accessible from common rolling surfaces, and aisle portions having related vertical pitches between rack levels.
counterfactuals.output:
1. **A storage rack array**, comprising:  
a plurality of storage rack structures arranged in a three-dimensional array and defining a plurality of vertically spaced rack levels, each rack level including a plurality of storage locations configured to receive inventory holders;  
a plurality of deck structures vertically spaced from one another and defining respective autonomous transport vehicle rolling surfaces, each rolling surface being configured to support travel of autonomous transport vehicles along at least one travel direction;  
wherein, at each of at least two of the rack levels, storage locations of a plurality of the storage rack structures are accessible by autonomous transport vehicles from a common one of the rolling surfaces;  
wherein the plurality of storage rack structures define aisle portions extending adjacent the storage locations, each aisle portion being associated with a corresponding rolling surface and providing vehicle access to storage locations at a corresponding rack level; and  
wherein a vertical pitch between first and second vertically adjacent rack levels differs from, is an integer multiple of, or is otherwise dimensionally related to a vertical pitch between first and second vertically adjacent rolling surfaces such that respective aisle portions of vertically adjacent rack levels are vertically registered with, vertically offset from, or vertically nested relative to one another to accommodate autonomous transport vehicle access to the storage locations from the common rolling surfaces.

2. **The storage rack array of claim 1**, wherein the plurality of deck structures comprise floor panels, rails, grating, plates, beams, or combinations thereof supported by the storage rack structures.

3. **The storage rack array of claim 1**, wherein each common rolling surface provides access to storage locations disposed on opposite lateral sides of a corresponding aisle portion.

4. **The storage rack array of claim 1**, wherein at least one rolling surface extends continuously across portions of multiple storage rack structures such that autonomous transport vehicles may travel between rack structures without leaving the rolling surface.

5. **The storage rack array of claim 1**, wherein the autonomous transport vehicle rolling surfaces are arranged at deck levels that are fewer in number than the rack levels, and wherein at least one rolling surface provides access to storage locations at more than one rack level.

6. **The storage rack array of claim 1**, wherein the vertical pitch between adjacent rack levels is substantially equal to a container height, tote height, pallet height, shelf opening height, or inventory-holder clearance height.

7. **The storage rack array of claim 1**, wherein the vertical pitch between adjacent rolling surfaces is greater than the vertical pitch between adjacent rack levels.

8. **The storage rack array of claim 7**, wherein the vertical pitch between adjacent rolling surfaces is substantially equal to an integer multiple of the vertical pitch between adjacent rack levels.

9. **The storage rack array of claim 1**, wherein at least one aisle portion includes a vehicle travel zone and a rack-access zone laterally adjacent the vehicle travel zone.

10. **The storage rack array of claim 1**, wherein the storage locations are arranged in columns and rows, and wherein the aisle portions are disposed between opposing rows of the storage locations.

11. **The storage rack array of claim 1**, wherein the autonomous transport vehicles are configured to roll on wheels directly supported by the rolling surfaces.

12. **The storage rack array of claim 1**, wherein the common rolling surface comprises a bi-directional or omni-directional travel surface permitting autonomous transport vehicles to access storage locations located at different lateral positions along the aisle portion.

13. **The storage rack array of claim 1**, wherein at least one of the rolling surfaces is disposed vertically between two rack levels and provides access to storage locations at both of the two rack levels.

14. **The storage rack array of claim 1**, wherein at least one rack level is accessible from a rolling surface positioned substantially coplanar with the rack level.

15. **The storage rack array of claim 1**, wherein the aisle portions of vertically adjacent rack levels have respective centerlines that are vertically aligned.

16. **The storage rack array of claim 1**, wherein the aisle portions of vertically adjacent rack levels have respective centerlines that are laterally offset.

17. **The storage rack array of claim 1**, wherein the dimensional relationship between the vertical pitches provides clearance for an autonomous transport vehicle traveling on a lower rolling surface beneath a rack level accessible from an upper rolling surface.

18. **The storage rack array of claim 1**, wherein the storage rack structures comprise uprights and horizontal support members, and wherein the deck structures are supported by at least some of the uprights.

19. **The storage rack array of claim 1**, further comprising at least one vertical transfer device configured to transfer an autonomous transport vehicle, an inventory holder, or both between the rolling surfaces.

20. **The storage rack array of claim 1**, wherein each rolling surface defines a common vehicle-access plane for a plurality of rack structures such that the autonomous transport vehicles may access storage locations of different rack structures from the same deck level without traversing a separate mezzanine, lift, or floor surface.

counterfactuals.output:
1. An automated storage and retrieval system comprising:

a plurality of storage racks arranged along at least one aisle, the storage racks defining storage locations at a plurality of vertical levels;

a plurality of deck structures disposed at respective ones of the vertical levels, each deck structure providing a travel surface configured to support travel of an autonomous vehicle along the at least one aisle; and

a control arrangement configured to cause the autonomous vehicle to perform an ordered picking operation from the storage locations,

wherein a rack pitch of the plurality of storage racks varies between different portions of the at least one aisle, such that a first aisle portion has a first rack pitch and a second aisle portion has a second rack pitch different from the first rack pitch, the varying rack pitch being arranged to coordinate the ordered picking operation by the autonomous vehicle.
